citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Fournier (Aix Marseille Univ, CNRS, LIS; IRD, ESPACE-DEV)
description: LUMA (Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal data) is a multimodal benchmark dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data. It includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages (~3 GB total), extending CIFAR-10/100 with audio samples from three corpora and text generated by the Gemma-7B LLM. The dataset enables controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty (aleatoric and epistemic) for benchmarking multimodal uncertainty quantification methods.
name: LUMA
rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 annotations per audio sample (for manual validation)
rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators total; described as colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 71.61% annotation agreement was achieved across the manually validated audio samples. Samples where both annotators agreed on validity were accepted (5,027 samples); samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Label Studio (academic license provided by HumanSignal team)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual audio validation used Label Studio. Annotators were shown each audio sample with the prompt "Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)" with answer options "Yes" or "No". Only samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted; samples with conflicting annotations were rejected. 8,372 samples were scheduled for manual labeling (only for classes with fewer than 800 samples after automatic validation).
rai:dataBiases: Gender bias was identified in LLM-generated texts, particularly for classes "man", "woman", "boy", and "girl". Examples of biased text included gender stereotypes (e.g., describing women as having "soft, nurturing personality" and taking care of family). Bias detection using Gemma-7B Instruct confirmed high levels of gender bias in these 4 classes. Prompts for these classes were reconstructed with explicit occupation-related keywords to reduce bias; after re-generation, enough unbiased texts (>800 per class) were available. The authors acknowledge the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases due to LLM generation, and state LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information.
rai:dataCollection: Images were compiled from CIFAR-10/100 (32x32 images), supplemented with EDM diffusion-generated images for diversity control. Audio samples were extracted from three corpora: The Spoken Wikipedia (phoneme-level aligned), LibriSpeech (force-aligned via Montreal Forced Aligner), and Mozilla Common Voice (force-aligned). 73 additional recordings for 4 classes were voluntarily contributed by colleagues. Text passages were generated using Google's Gemma-7B Instruct LLM with 13 different prompts per class label. Each modality was independently sourced and then aligned across modalities.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images: CIFAR-10/100 dataset (32x32 images) and EDM diffusion-generated images. Audio: The Spoken Wikipedia corpus (hundreds of hours of phoneme-level aligned audio), LibriSpeech corpus (1,000 hours of English speech from audiobooks), and Mozilla Common Voice (crowdsourced open-source voice collection). Text: Generated by Gemma-7B Instruct LLM using 13 prompt templates per class label.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Others
rai:dataLimitations: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. Audio samples from forced alignments may contain misaligned segments introducing additional noise. Some audio samples from voluntary contributions may be very noisy or have strong accents. The dataset currently lacks dependent modalities, limiting comprehensive uncertainty quantification studies.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The Python toolkit supports controlled injection of uncertainty: (1) Data diversity control — deep features extracted (Wav2Vec for audio, BERT for text, VGG-11 for images) and samples drawn from a categorical distribution weighted by inverse distance to class center raised to power k; (2) Sample noise injection — background noise from ESC-50 added to audio via audiomentations library; text noise via nlpaug (keyboard, OCR, random character, antonym, random word, spelling, back-translation); image noise via 15 perturbation types (Gaussian noise, shot noise, impulse noise, blurs, weather effects, etc.); (3) Label noise injection — labels randomly reassigned to semantically close classes based on deep feature distances to nearest neighbors; (4) OOD injection — 8 classes held out as OOD samples.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio: Word-level alignments were generated using Montreal Forced Aligner for LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice. Audio segments corresponding to CIFAR class labels (including plural forms) were extracted. Automatic validation used OpenAI Whisper Large V3 for transcription; 130,069 out of 178,123 samples were auto-validated. Remaining samples underwent manual validation. Text: Generated texts were validated by masking label occurrences and re-feeding into Gemma-7B Instruct for classification; 55,953 text samples were accepted. For 4 classes (man, woman, boy, girl), prompts were reconstructed to reduce gender bias, and bias detection was re-run. Images: 42 classes with ≥600 validated samples were used as in-distribution; 8 classes with fewer samples were designated OOD.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote development of trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety-critical applications such as healthcare and autonomous driving. The authors anticipate LUMA will help the research community design more trustworthy and robust ML approaches. The dataset contains LLM-generated text with potential gender biases and stereotypes, which the authors identified and partially mitigated through prompt reconstruction.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal uncertainty quantification (MUQ) methods; studying aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in multimodal deep learning; evaluating model robustness to noise; out-of-distribution (OOD) detection research; developing trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches for safety-critical applications (e.g., healthcare, autonomous driving).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3 (used for automatic audio transcription and validation — 130,069 out of 178,123 samples validated automatically). Gemma-7B Instruct (used for text generation and for text validation by masked label classification, and for bias detection). Montreal Forced Aligner (used to generate word-level alignments for LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice audio).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: 73 audio recordings voluntarily contributed by colleagues were anonymized before inclusion in the dataset.
